verb_forms.resultant_states.rule: Be + an established participial adjective can describe a present state: be gone (absent), be finished (done). Do not generalise be to all motion verbs. Contrast has gone (present perfect, departure with present relevance); she has gone for her break is natural. Do not treat both forms as interchangeable in every context.
good: Are you finished with the report?
verb_forms.resultant_states.wrong: He is left for work. (use has left)

subjunctive.present_wishes.rule: Wish + past form expresses a present situation one wants to be different. After I/he/she/it both was and were are grammatical; were is more formal. Accept both when context permits. Distinguish wishes about the past (past perfect).
good: I wish I knew the answer.
subjunctive.present_wishes.wrong: I wish I know the answer. (present unreal wish)
